ops.body: - [owner] The destructive button is a filled red slab in every confirm (a walk's "Delete walk" and "Remove", `ConfirmCard`) and in the three "Discard these edits?" asks (`WalkActions.tsx`, `replay/[id].tsx`, `edit/MediaEditor.tsx`), heavier than either platform draws it: iOS gives the destructive item red text on a plain row with Cancel in bold, Material two text buttons of equal weight that let the words do the work (the reviewer's precedent, recorded in `docs/research/ui-references.md` A5 on Nov 18: the system red verified, the bold Cancel and Material's equal weight unverified). Rests on `docs/research/ui-references.md` B3 ("Don't assign the primary role to a button that performs a destructive action") and its goal-to-control matrix, row 8 (Avoid: "a destructive default or primary button"). Stacked at 320 px since `tend deletion 1` it is the first and most saturated thing in the card. A cross-screen call: red text with a red outline and Cancel the stronger style, in every confirm at once so they stay alike (the `tend deletion 1` review's ux U3, Nov 18, low; there before this run)
